problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t),$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{4}{5}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{5}\,\text{s}.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. Given that it is at rest when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0)+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).$
